label: rem:flavor-charge-assignments
title: Flavor charge assignments and the hypercharge gap
html:
Remark. Flavor charge assignments and the hypercharge gap

The A_2 weight lattice of the A_2 proposition assigns two quantum numbers to each state: the third component of isospin I_3 and the hypercharge Y, related to the fundamental weights by

  I_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2),
  \qquad
  Y   = \tfrac{1}{3}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2).

The electric charge is then the Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation Q = I_3 + Y/2.

Derived quantity: isospin I_3. The writhe-to-isospin map w \mapsto I_3 is derived in the framework without fitted parameters. Over the nucleon doublet, the proton braid \mathfrak{p} and neutron braid \mathfrak{n} carry writhes whose difference reproduces \Delta I_3 = 1 scale-free. This identifies I_3 as the writhe coordinate on the A_2 weight lattice.

Open quantity: hypercharge Y. The writhe map is falsified as a hypercharge assignment: the proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ. The framework therefore requires a second crossing invariant, independent of the writhe, to instantiate Y.

The candidate direction, recorded without endorsement, is the ribbon-framing twist. In the categorical braid representation, each strand carries a framing datum whose total T(t) is independent of the crossing word (hence independent of the writhe w). The candidate hypercharge is

  Y_t = 2\bigl(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3\bigr),
  \qquad
  Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = \frac{T(t)}{3},

where T(t)/3 is the colour-tube charge quantum of the quark picture (the helon-model normalisation [bilson-thompson2005]). The Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation holds by construction if and only if Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q against the crossing-derived Coulomb charge Q = w/2 --- a falsifiable consistency condition, not a definition.

Status and batteries. Neither the candidate nor any alternative has been wired. Any hypercharge proposal must pass two batteries before instantiating the class:

  1. Gell-Mann--Nishijima consistency: Q = I_3 + Y/2 must hold against the independently derived Q and I_3 on the nucleon doublet, without tuning a coupling.
  2. First-generation spectrum: The Y values of u, d, e^-, \nu_e must reproduce \{+1/3, +1/3, -1, -1\} (left-handed) and \{+4/3, -2/3, -2, 0\} (right-handed), satisfying the \mathbb{Z}_6 compatibility relations [baez-huerta2010].

A candidate requiring a fitted scale to pass either battery is a fit, not a derivation, and does not instantiate this class.

Enumeration result, and why it carries no corroboration. The battery has been run over all 10{,}000 helon-style assignments (3 strands per fermion, per-strand twist in \{-1, 0, +1\}), of which 4 survive. That ratio must not be read as a 2500\!:\!1 filter: the battery collapses to a single linear equation per flavour, and the surviving count is multiset counting. Proved sorry-free in QOU/StandardModel/TwistBatteryVacuity.lean:

  1. The spectrum battery is exactly T = 3Q. Both the candidate Y_t = 2(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3) and the target Y = 2(Q - I_3) carry the same -2I_3, which cancels. What remains is Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q --- the defining equation of Q_{\mathrm{twist}}, not a test of it. The battery constrains nothing about isospin.
  2. The nucleon-doublet check is entailed, by charge additivity alone: T_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2T_u + T_d = 3(2Q_u + Q_d) follows from T = 3Q on the quarks, so no surviving assignment can fail it. As implemented it also states one condition twice --- its second clause 2(T_{\mathfrak{p}}/3 - 1/2) = 1 clears to T_{\mathfrak{p}} = 3, which is its own first clause.
  3. The \mathbb{Z}_6 condition is not a filter. In strand_twist_y_battery.py it is a function of the Standard-Model table alone and never sees the candidate assignment; it runs as an input assertion and cannot exclude any multiset.

So each flavour is filtered independently by one equation, and 4 = 1 \times 2 \times 2 \times 1 counts the multisets of three twists from \{-1,0,+1\} with the required totals 3Q = (2, -1, 0, -3). The u-quark twist \{0,1,1\} and the electron twist \{-1,-1,-1\} are the two totals admitting a single multiset --- a fact about writing 2 and -3 as a sum of three elements of \{-1,0,+1\}, not about the framework; the d-quark and neutrino each admit two. Passing the battery is therefore equivalent to choosing t with \sum_i t_i = 3Q, which is always possible.

The open content is unchanged and is the whole question: whether the twist multisets are forced by the framework's braid words rather than only consistent with them. See strand-twist-y-battery.witness.json.

A derived-twist repair, tested and refuted (scope-(a)). The defect above is that t is a free label. The natural repair is to replace it with the canonical twist of the ribbon category --- on a simple object the twist acts by a scalar whose exponent is the content sum c(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} (j - i), a derived per-block integer. Taking Q = c(\lambda)/3 is parameter-free. It does not work: at n = 3 the content sums are \{3, 0, -3\}, giving the integer charges \{+1, 0, -1\} with no third-integer charge at all, and no n \le 8 yields both quark charges \{+2/3, -1/3\} (ribbon_twist_charge_quantum_probe.py). This is scope-(a) for the plain content-sum reading, not an exclusion of the ribbon route: other normalisations remain untested.
